pr_body:
Make meilisearch support JWT authentication signed with meilisearch API keys
using HS256, HS384 or HS512 algorithms.

Related spec: [specifications#89](https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/89) [rendered](https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/blob/scoped-api-keys/text/0089-tenant-tokens.md)
Fix #1991

Check the spec and the PR description (#2096) for more details
comments: Sorry, I forgot to ping both teams: @meilisearch/integration-team and @meilisearch/docs-team

review_comments: Could you document this struct, please?
Why are you first checking that a key can do something and then chack that the key is valid? Why not in the other order?
in `is_key_authorized` we have LMDB accesses to check key authorization, in `is_key_valid` we have a sha256 digest, I chose to do the hash at the end. I can change the order if you want. ☺️
No!! this function in blocking, you can't call it in this context! You need to make them async again, and call the store operation from a `tokio::spawn_blocking` context
Does this mean that `bearer` (without the capitalization) will not be detected?
Only "Bearer" written with a capital is accepted, with exactly one space between it and the following key.
uhm that is not http compliant: https://stackoverflow.com/a/5259004
@MarinPostma @Kerollmops, "Bearer" is not the Header name but a part of the Value, the header name is "Authentication".

I don't know if it's the good RFC, but, here is a pseudo regex matching the bearer auth:
[The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework: Bearer Token Usage](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750#section-2.1)
If it is a real issue can you "Reference in a new issue", please? If it is not, let's merge that and pray!
There is no issue here, I don't understand your point. 😞
I'll find a way to not depend on meilisearch auth here later, so that's ok for now
Could you document this struct, please?
